You can place detector response functions imported from GADRAS-DRF into InterSpecs directory within the Files app.

These are detector response functions imported from GADRAS-DRF. The crystal shape and material, dead layer, endcap attenuators, setback, FWHM and peak shape are all read from Detector.dat, and the efficiency from Efficiency.csv. A directory holding only a Detector.dat is listed as "geometry only": picking it opens the Monte-Carlo characterization that gives it an efficiency. Coaxial bore geometry and partial side or back shields are not recorded by the format, so they are not modeled.

Detector efficiency defined by a mathematical formula, given the energy x; or you can enter the coefficients for the standard equation form. Click the question mark icon for more info.:

How this efficiency should be interpreted.
Intrinsic Efficiency: the probability for a x-ray or gamma striking the face of the detector, to register a full-energy detection event.
Absolute Efficiency: the probability for a x-ray or gamma from the source to register a full-energy detection event, with it being appropriate to allow scaling this efficiency by 1/r2 to other distances (i.g., is for a point-source).
Fixed Geometry - total activity: the probability for a x-ray or gamma from the source to register a full-energy detection event, and it is not appropriate to allow scaling this efficiency to other distances (e.g., for a near, or large extended source).
Fixed Geometry - activity per cm2: similar to total activity, but the efficiency curve represents efficiency per decay, per square centimeter (i.e., surface contamination).
Fixed Geometry - activity per m2: similar to per cm2, but for per square meter.
Fixed Geometry - activity per g: similar to per cm2, but for per gram of source.

This link carries the detector geometry, but not Monte-Carlo characterization. When read-in it will need re-generating (the XML download avoids this).
Received detector efficiency contains the detector geometry.
The geometry is saved with the detector, but not used. Efficiencies are only right at the distance and angle the detector was characterized at.
Recommended. Uses the geometry to correct the efficiency curve for sources off to the side, or close to the detector. Instant, and the same thing a GADRAS Detector.dat import does.
Simulates the on-axis energies plus a few off-axis angles, and uses the geometry to carry those to other distances. About a tenth the work of a full run.
Simulates radiation through the detector across distances and angles. Takes minutes; opens in Modify Detector Response, where you can watch its progress or cancel it.
As Standard, with extra detail very close to the detector. The slowest option; opens in Modify Detector Response, where you can watch its progress or cancel it.
Could not start the Monte-Carlo generation - the detector is in use with its efficiency curve. You can retry from the "Geom & MC" tab of Modify Detector Response.
Efficiency is intrinsic (per gamma striking the detector face); solid-angle corrections are applied for the source distance.
Efficiency is for one specific source/detector geometry - distances do not apply.
Efficiency uncertainties (used to propagate detector uncertainty into fit results). This detector reports none, so an activity fit with it will report counting statistics only.
Efficiency uncertainty, as an activity fit propagates it: {2}% at {1} keV, all of it supported by this detector's own data.

Efficiency uncertainty, as an activity fit propagates it: {2}% at {1} keV - but none of it is a measurement of this detector. {3}% is the default assumed for a detector that states no uncertainty of its own (a GADRAS Detector.dat, for example), and {4}% is the model envelope. "Modify..." lets you enter what you actually know.

Efficiency uncertainty, as an activity fit propagates it: {2}% at {1} keV - {3}% from this detector's own data, and {4}% model envelope: an allowance for asking the model about a position nobody measured. The envelope does not shrink with more counting, and it moves every peak together.
Total efficiency (probability of depositing any energy) - the input needed for cascade-summing corrections. This detector has none, so cascade-summing corrections are unavailable.
Total-efficiency curve (probability of depositing any energy; input for cascade-summing corrections).
Total efficiency (probability of depositing any energy; input for cascade-summing corrections), supplied by this detector's Monte-Carlo response rather than by a separate curve.
The raw per-peak efficiency measurements this DRF was made from (kept for provenance, and to anchor a Monte-Carlo characterization).
Full Monte-Carlo-parameterized response ({1} profile; valid {2}-{3} keV): off-axis and near-field efficiencies with honest uncertainties.
No Monte-Carlo parameterization - efficiencies are on-axis far-field only. Use "Characterize by MC..." to add one.

Efficiency-transfer response (an anchored efficiency curve carried to other distances/angles through the exact ray-traced detector geometry; valid {1}-{2} keV). Best accuracy on-axis at distances beyond {3}; closer or well off-axis queries are flagged and carry an honestly inflated uncertainty. For the best near-field / off-axis accuracy run a Full MC characterization ("Modify...", Geom & MC tab).

Whether the Monte-Carlo response has been anchored to measured efficiencies (k(E) correction with covariance). "(curve)" means it was anchored to a fitted curve rather than raw measured points - slightly lower quality.
